full_judgment:
2. Short facts necessary for disposal of these appeals are that the appellants in C.A No. 111 of 2006 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.03 of 1991 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge 3rd Court, Dhaka for declaratory decree and for permanent injunction. 

 4. The trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 29.08.1999 decreed the suit, declared the deed described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint cancelled and also passed a decree for permanent injunction restraining defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from creating any obstacle in the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the 'ka' scheduled land. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendants filed Title Appeal No.623 of 1999 before, the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Joint District Judge and Artha Bin Adalat No.4, Dhaka by the judgment and decree dated 11.10.2001 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiffs preferred Civil Revision No.6307 of 2001 before the High Court Division. A learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute, set aside the judgments and decrees of the Courts below and sent the suit on remand to the trial Court for fresh trial. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the plaintiffs filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 507 of 2005 before this Court and leave was granted giving rise to Civil Appeal No.111 of 2006. The defendants also filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1632 of 2005 and leave was granted by this Court giving rise to Civil Appeal No. 102 of 2007. 

 5. Heard Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, learned Counsel for the appellants in Civil Appeal No.111 of 2006 as well as respondent Nos.1 and 2 in Civil Appeal No.102 of 2007 and Mrs. Nahid Yesmin, learned Advocate for respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in Civil Appeal No.111 of 2006 and appellants  in Civil Appeal No.102 of 2007 and perused the judgments and decrees of the Courts below and the impugned judgment and order.
